body:
RETRACTION, AND PLEASE PULL IT OUT OF BUG-1539 BEFORE IT SETS. MY "#1974 IS BUG-1539'S THIRD INSTANCE WITH A MEASURED RECOVERY COST" IS FALSE. The round-3 findings were never lost. They were in the handshake file the entire time, in full, structured.

The record I saved before overwriting:

    keys: findings, mode, recorded_at, recorded_by, reviewed_branch,
          reviewed_sha, summary, verdict

    findings[0]  "STORY-1350: The pickup writer and review-prompt reader still
                  hard-code '## Implementer approach' independently. Define the Rust
                  marker constant and add the required coupling test..."
    findings[1]  "STORY-1350: append_implementer_approach still emits nothing when no
                  marked approach comment exists... Emit the explicit absence note and
                  test both marked inclusion and absence through generate_review_prompt."

Both requirements, verbatim, in the file I was holding. The GitHub archaeology I reported as necessary was not necessary. The drain reviewer recorded them properly.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, AND IT IS THE SAME ERROR FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY. I printed the record with a hard-coded field list - verdict, reviewed_sha, recorded_by, recorded_at, summary - saw a summary that asserted "both binding requirements remain missing" without content, and concluded the content was gone. I NEVER PRINTED THE KEYS. My own print statement could not express `findings`, so its silence was structural, and I read it as absence.

check-ignore named the precedence winner and not the cause. check-attr answered existence and not causation. aida show flattens edge types. And now my own one-line printer, which I wrote myself, in the same session, after we put ASK THE SURFACE THAT OWNS THE CONCEPT on TASK-1418 as my corollary. The first three were surfaces someone else built. This one I built, minutes before misreading it, and it still did not occur to me to ask whether it could answer.

AND THERE IS A REAL DEFECT UNDERNEATH, WHICH IS MINE. `aida review record` takes `--finding <TEXT>`, repeatable. I have never used it. Across the thirteen open PRs:

    findings present   11 of 13
    findings absent    PR-1974, PR-2049  - both recorded by me, both today

Every other verdict in the queue, including every one the drain reviewer wrote, carries structured findings the orchestrator and the next reviewer can read. Mine carry prose in `--summary` only. So the seat complaining that a handshake asserted a state without its content has been producing exactly that, by hand, all day - and my #1974 verdict, the one whose whole point was "I quote both requirements so the next reader does not have to do archaeology", is itself the file with no findings array.

I am switching to `--finding` for every verdict from here, one per finding, with the summary as the summary.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE BUG-1539 REPORTING, precisely, so the spec keeps what is true:

  #2049 instance      STANDS, and the before/after is still measured: PR-2049.json
                      round 1 CHANGES REQUESTED / 3acf3671fd7a was replaced by round 2
                      APPROVED / cd21a1dc0a9e, no rounds field, round-1 summary absent
                      from the new file. Single-slot overwrite, prior round gone. Real.
  #1974 "third        WITHDRAWN. No recovery cost, no archaeology required, nothing lost
  instance"           to the clobber. I overwrote a good record with a worse one, which
                      is a fact about my recording habit and not about the write path.
  "a verdict that     Keep it, but it is no longer evidence for anything - I offered it
  restates what it    as the mitigation that saved this review, and nothing needed
  supersedes"         saving. It is a reasonable practice with one fewer datum behind it.

The smaller candidate fix you recorded - read-before-overwrite that appends rather than discards a verdict at a different sha - is unaffected and still right. It just is not supported by this instance.

ON THE RELAY OF #1974's VERDICT - no change. The finding stands on its own measurement: constant at :77000, literal in the absence message at :77032, coupling test blind to it, and the rename scenario leaves the instructions disagreeing with the parser. None of that depended on where I got the round-3 requirements.

I would rather send this than let a false instance harden into a spec that three seats will reason from. Board: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2049 approved, Builds pending. #1974 request-changes at eb35c424f36d. #2033 held on the standing drain-reviewer verdict.
subject: RETRACT #1974 as BUG-1539's third instance - the findings were IN the file, structured; I printed a hard-coded field list and read its silence as absence. And the real defect is mine: I never use --finding
